paper_title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Small language models are usually built like large ones and then squeezed onto a CPU afterwards. We did the opposite: we fixed the target first, one user, one token at a time, 4-bit weights, ordinary CPU, and chose the architecture to suit it. The result keeps full attention in only 6 of its 18 blocks. The other 12 use short convolutions whose memory is two timesteps wide no matter how long the conversation gets, so two thirds of the network never re-reads a growing cache. Trained from scratch on 59.9B tokens, the model scores 47.31 on a five-task benchmark against a bar of 42.20 that was fixed before training began. It beats GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M and GPT-neo-125M, all trained on three to six times more data, and exceeds MobileLLM-125M's published score despite that model seeing a trillion tokens. Validation bits-per-byte is 0.8685. To check the architecture rather than the training recipe, we trained a conventional all-attention model of the same size on the same data, and wrote down the winning condition before scoring either. The hybrid won the chosen quality metric by 0.81%, matched it on downstream tasks, produced a 6.3% smaller 4-bit file, and decoded 1.76x faster at 2048 tokens of context, 2.08x against an external model of similar size. In every measurement the speed advantage is near zero at an empty context and grows with length, which is what the mechanism predicts and what a merely leaner model would not show. A simple bandwidth calculation predicts only 1.17x, so memory volume alone does not explain the gap. We also report what did not work: an unmitigated 4-bit quality cost, roughly half the convolution channels ending up inert and impossible to remove, and a vocabulary larger than this model size warrants.

The hybrid won the chosen quality metric by 0.81 %, matched it on downstream tasks, produced 6.3 % smaller 4-bit file, and decoded 1.76 faster at 2048 tokens of context 2.08 against an external model of similar size. In every measurement the speed advantage is near zero at an empty context and grows with length, which is what the mechanism predicts and what merely leaner model would not show. simple bandwidth calculation predicts only 1.17, so memory volume alone does not explain the gap. We also report what did not work: an unmitigated 4-bit quality cost, roughly half the convolution channels ending up inert and impossible to remove, and vocabulary larger than this model size warrants. Index Termslanguage models, CPU inference, efficient architectures, hybrid models, quantisation, memory bandwidth, edge deployment I. INTRODUCTION language model serving single user on CPU is not smaller version of model serving many users on GPU. Three properties of the regime differ, and together they change what an efficient architecture looks like. Batch size is one. There is no batching over which to amortise weight loading. Every decoded token requires streaming the models weights through the memory hierarchy, so throughput is governed by bytes read per token rather than by arithmetic throughput. Memory bandwidth binds before compute. contemporary CPU can issue far more arithmetic than it can feed with operands. This inverts the usual optimisation target: an architecture performing more arithmetic over fewer bytes runs faster. The keyvalue cache is growing tax. In an all-attention decoder, generating each token requires re-reading the keys and values of every preceding token in every layer. That cost is linear in context length and is paid per token. Under highbandwidth, large-batch GPU serving it is tolerable; at batch size one on CPU it dominates long-context decoding. The last property is the design lever this work pulls. If most layers carry constant-size state rather than growing one, decode cost becomes far flatter in context length, and the advantage widens precisely where users perceive latency: long conversations and long documents. A. Contributions 1) concrete sub-200M architecture whose layer composition is chosen from CPU memory-traffic argument rather than adapted from GPU practice. 2) pre-registered, parameter-matched ablation isolating the effect of that composition, with the decision rule fixed before either arm was scored. 3) Decode measurements at three context depths against both an internal twin and an external peer, showing the advantage grows with depth in both. 4) first-order cost model that under-predicts the measured advantage, localising the residual to latency rather than bandwidth. 5) negative result closing structural pruning of dead convolution channels, and full account of five deviations forced on the training run. B. Success criteria fixed in advance To prevent post-hoc rationalisation, the evaluation bar was fixed by operator decision before any headline number existed. Quality is the five-task mean over HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, PIQA, OpenBookQA and WinoGrande, scored under lmevaluation-harness conventions on single harness so that peers and this model are measured identically. Table lists the comparison set. The bar is 42.2, the strongest of the four beatable peers. Clearing it means matching or exceeding 300 B-token-class models on roughly seven times less data. The second half of the barCPU decode speedis an architectural property and does not depend on training outcome. II. SCORES ARE MEASURED ON THIS PROJECTS HARNESS, NOT QUOTED FROM PUBLICATIONS. A. The short-convolution block

sections.content: Model Tokens 5-task Target Pythia-160M GPT-neo-125M OPT-125M GPT-2 124M MobileLLM-125M Peer-135M 300 300 180 1 2 41.0 41.9 42.1 42.2 gated 51.2 beat beat beat the bar stretch concede quality budgets when trained on carefully filtered data. Pythia [6] established reproducible small baselines; MobileLLM [7] showed that depth-over-width and embedding sharing matter disproportionately below 350 parameters, finding this design adopts in its narrow feed-forward and tied embeddings. Recurrent and hybrid sequence models. Structured statespace models [8] and gated linear-recurrent architectures [9] replace attention with mechanisms whose inference state is constant in sequence length. Purely recurrent models, however, lose the precise associative recall that attention provides. Hybrids that retain minority of attention layersGriffin [10] being prominent examplerecover most of that capability while keeping the majority of layers cache-free. Daedalus sits in this family, with two distinguishing choices: the recurrent operator is very short depthwise convolution rather than selective-scan state-space layer, chosen because it maps onto existing CPU inference kernels without new operators; and the attention-to-recurrence ratio is fixed by memory-traffic argument specific to batch-size-one CPU decoding. Efficient attention. Multi-query and grouped-query attention [3] shrink the cache by sharing keyvalue heads across query heads. This is complementary rather than alternative: Daedalus applies GQA to the six attention layers it retains, compounding the two reductions. Quantisation. Post-training quantisation to 4 bits is standard for CPU deployment. We target the reference runtimes [5] Q4_0 format specifically because its dot-product kernels are the best optimised on the target hardware, rather than format with better theoretical error at lower throughput. What is new here. The contribution is not new operator. It is the observation that in the batch-size-one CPU regime the ratio of cache-free to attention layers is the dominant deployable design variable, together with controlled experiment that isolates its effect at matched parameter count. III. ARCHITECTURE Daedalus-150M has 160.49 parameters in 18 blocks at dmodel = 768, feed-forward inner dimension 2048, vocabulary 49,152 and context 2048. Six blocks use full attention and twelve use short convolutions, interleaved as

V. CORPUS AND DATA PIPELINE Training data is ten-source English mixture totalling 16.93 unique tokens, weighted toward educational and reasoning-dense text (Table III). At this scale data quality dominates quantity, and the evaluation suite is knowledgeand commonsense-heavy. A. Bounded repetition 59.9 B-token budget over 16.93 B-token corpus implies roughly 3.5 epochs. Rather than allow any source to be repeated arbitrarily to meet its nominal share, each source is capped at four epochs, following the finding that repetition up to approximately four epochs costs little relative to unique data [2]. Mass freed by capped source is redistributed by water-filling across sources retaining headroom. The cap is load-bearing. Without it, source such as everyday-conversations (approximately 400 tokens) would be repeated thousands of times to fill 2 % share, which is not what 2 % share is meant to express. B. Packing and held-out data Documents are tokenised and packed into fixed-size shards of contiguous token ids. Each source reserves whole shard filesnever token slicesfor 2 % holdout, so no training window can straddle the train/holdout boundary. Because shard files are reserved whole, the realised holdout fraction varies per source: source whose trailing shard is small relative to the target must reserve the preceding shard too, and one sources real carve is 9.16 % rather than 2 %. Uneven carves perturb the training mixture, so the effect is measured rather than assumed. Validation bits-per-byte is weighted by the probabilities the sampler actually draws with, not by holdout token counts. Correcting this distinction changed the reported metric by 9.7 %: weighting by holdout size systematically over-weighted the hardest sources, because those sources happened to have larger trailing shards. VI. TRAINING Table IV summarises the configuration. Parameters are split by tensor shape: two-dimensional weight matrices are optimised by Muon [4], and embeddings, norms and biases by AdamW122.68 parameters over 102 tensors and 37.81 over 62 respectively. A. Decaying the learning rate to zero The schedule is warmupstabledecay with linear decay to zero, not cosine decay to floor, following evidence that full decay to zero is substantially more sample-efficient [1]. practical consequence deserves emphasis for anyone reading the loss curve: training loss is expected to plateau during the stable phase. Between approximately step 20,000 and step 68,461 the learning rate is held at its peak and loss moves very little. This is the schedule operating as designed, not stall; nearly all remaining quality is purchased during the decay phase. In this run the plateau was mistaken for stall by an observer, which is precisely why it is documented here. secondary benefit is that the checkpoint at the onset of decay is reusable branch point: it can be trained further on additional or different data and re-decayed, whereas model already annealed to lr 0 requires learning-rate re-warmup. VII. CENTRAL EXPERIMENT: HYBRID VERSUS DENSE The architectural claim was tested directly, with the decision rule fixed before either arm was scored. Two models, parameter-matched to within 0.5 % (160.49 hybrid against 161.25 dense, the twin being 24 all-attention layers at = 640 with feed-forward 2304), were trained on identical data and schedule for 5 tokens each and fully decayed. The pre-registered metric was validation bits-per-byte over 645 M-token held-out set with 0.5 % margin floor fixed in advance. dense win beyond that floor was live possible outcome that would have changed the main runs architecture. A. Quality The hybrid wins the pre-registered metric by 0.81 %, clearing the 0.5 % floor. On the five-task mean the dense twin is nominally ahead by 0.14 points, approximately 0.24σ against the 0.58σ these suites carry. Validation bits-per-byte, computed over 645 held-out tokens, separates architectures far more sensitively at this scale, which is why it was pre-registered. The honest summary is that the hybrid matches on quality and wins decisively on decode. It is not downstream-task win, and is not presented as one. B. Per-domain difficulty Table VI decomposes validation bits-per-byte by source for the dense arm. The spread is nearly factor of two and is informative for anyone reusing this corpus: code and encyclopedic text are far more predictable than broad filtered web text, so an aggregate figure is dominated by the mixture weights as much as by the model. C. CPU decode speed Decode is measured with 4-bit weights on 8 threads, generating 128 tokens after priming context of the stated depth. Arms alternate within single pass so that background load on the measurement machine perturbs both equally; the ratio within pass is therefore more trustworthy than the absolute throughputs, which are depressed by whatever else is running. Table VII contains the central result, and its shape is the thesis. At depth zero the hybrid has almost nothing to gain, because its advantage is the cache it does not keep and an empty context has no cache to re-read. The advantage grows monotonically with context, reaching 1.76 at the trained context length. One confound runs against the hybrid: the dense twin receives the reference runtimes better-optimised attention graph, which has had far more engineering attention than the hybrids convolution path. Fig. 2 plots the same data. The two curves do not merely differ by constant: they diverge, and the divergence is the quantity the architecture was designed to produce. D. Comparison against an external peer Daedalus decodes 2.08 faster at the context it is built for while carrying 19 % more parameters. The same signature near unity at depth zero, growing with contextreproduces against different architecture written by different author, which is stronger evidence for the mechanism than the withinproject comparison alone, since it cannot be an artefact of this projects training or export code. Matched within 0.5 % at half precision (306.22 MiB against 307.63 MiB), the hybrids shipped file is 95.56 MiB against the twins 101.62 MiB6.3 % smaller, at 4.99 versus 5.29 bits per weight. That clears the 42.2 bar and exceeds all four 300 B-token-class peers on every one of the five tasks. HEADLINE RESULTS Table IX gives the finished model measured on the harness described in Section XI, alongside the peers it was required to beat. The model clears the 42.20 bar by 5.11 points and beats it was set against, each of which saw three every model to six times more data. It also exceeds MobileLLM-125Ms published figure, which came from trillion tokens. The 2 T-token peer in the last row remains ahead by 3.9 points. That was conceded before training started: this project trades quality against decode speed at fixed size, and Section VII-C is the other half of that trade. Validation bits-per-byte over 645 M-token held-out set is 0.8685. The same architecture trained on 5 tokens reached 0.9104, so the remaining 55 tokens bought 4.6 % improvement large gain by the standards of this metric, which moves slowly. Quantising to 4 bits costs roughly 6 % perplexity (9.18 at half precision against 9.75 at Q4_0, measured on held-out encyclopedic text). That is higher than the 2.5 % measured at 5 tokens and is discussed in Section IX-C. PIQA ARC-Easy WinoGrande HellaSwag OpenBookQA Mean 65.78 50.42 50.04 37.93 32.40 47.31 50.0 25.0 50.0 25.0 25.0 IX. LIMITATIONS A. The training mixture drifted from its target The corpus holds 16.9 unique tokens and the run consumed 59.9 B, so most text is seen about three and half times. Each source is capped at four repetitions, and for the largest sources that cap binds their share cannot be met without exceeding it, so the freed share flows to smaller sources that still have unread text. The realised mixture therefore sits some distance from the intended one. Measured as L1 distance in percentage points, the run as whole is at 10.42 against limit of 10.0 that was fixed in advance. The largest single-source deviation is 0.24 points, which is negligible against benchmark noise, but the headline figure is over the limit and is reported as such. If downstream results ever look weaker than the peer comparison suggests they should, mixture drift is live explanation. B. The last 8 % of training used slightly smaller corpus Training was interrupted and resumed from checkpoint. Three consequences are permanent properties of the released weights and are stated rather than smoothed over. The optimiser state was not carried across: momentum restarted from zero and re-warmed over few hundred steps. This is mild by that point the learning rate had already decayed to 0.0035 but the run is not one continuous optimiser trajectory. The data cursor also reset, so the final 4.8 tokens are fresh pass over the corpus rather than continuation. Some documents were seen twice and some not at all. Those tokens came from corpus snapshot 0.42 tokens smaller than the one used earlier, which is what pushed the mixture figure above from 9.94 to 10.42. C. Quantisation-aware training did not run The plan was to spend the final 5 % of training with fake quantisation applied on the deployment formats exact 4-bit grid, verified against the runtimes own kernel rather than reimplemented. It produced non-finite loss on its first step and was disabled; the run finished without it. The released model is therefore quantised after training rather than during it, and carries the full 4-bit penalty about 6 % perplexity rather than the 2.5 % measured at smaller scale. The half-precision weights are published, so this is fixable without repeating any training: either by running the quantisation-aware pass from the finished checkpoint, or by choosing format with better error behaviour at the same bit width. We did not diagnose the failure. D. The vocabulary is larger than this size warrants The tokeniser, and with it 49,152-entry vocabulary, was adopted from an existing model because an earlier plan required student and teacher to share one exactly. That plan was dropped for unrelated reasons; the vocabulary stayed. Scaling laws put the optimum for 150 model nearer 24 32 k. At 49,152 the embedding table holds 37.7 parameters 23 % of the model where 32 vocabulary would hold 24.6 M, freeing roughly 13 parameters for layers that compute rather than look up. Tied embeddings recover half the waste, which is probably why it was never revisited. smaller vocabulary is the first thing to change in successor. We did verify the tokeniser rather than assume it: reading token ids directly out of the quantised file gave zero mismatches against the reference tokeniser. silent mismatch here ships model that produces fluent nonsense while every reported metric looks healthy, and nothing else in the pipeline would catch it. E. Single seed, English only Every number here comes from one seed. The 0.81 % ablation margin is not confidence interval, and the downstream comparison is reported as tie partly because one seed cannot resolve quarter of standard deviation. The model is Englishonly, and the decode advantage is measured at the 2048-token context it was trained for, not extrapolated past it. X. NEGATIVE RESULT: DEAD CHANNELS CANNOT BE RECLAIMED Approximately 47.9 % of short-convolution channels contribute nothing to the models output. This is stable plateau rather than progressive decay: the fraction measures 47.928 % at step 9,896 and 47.993 % at step 30,041, and is unchanged over the following 10,743 steps. It represents roughly 13.6 inert parameters, an 8.5 % parameter inefficiency. Because the mask is stable and the convolution is depthwise, structural pruning at export appeared straightforward: narrow each blocks projections and kernel while leaving the residual stream at full width, for an estimated 7.7 MB saving. This was tested and does not work. The reference runtime creates all three short-convolution tensors at fixed model width and shape-checks them at load time; real artefact narrowed from 768 to 640 is rejected with check_tensor_dims: expected 3,768, got 3,640, while both the unmodified file and the same file rebuilt at full width through the identical writer load correctly. That second control is what makes the finding conclusive: the rejection is the narrowing itself, not an artefact of the rewriting tool. the

sections.title: Reclaiming
sections.content: patching parameters would the inference runtime, which would forfeit stock-binary compatibilitythe foundation of the CPU-decode claimin exchange for 7.7 MB. Four-bit quantisation moreover spends require four bits on zero exactly as on any other weight, so the inert channels cost nothing beyond their share of the file. The appropriate remedy belongs to the next models initialisation and regularisation, not to retrofit of this one. XI. EVALUATION METHODOLOGY Because several claims in this paper are comparative, the instruments deserve description. A. Quality The five-task suite is scored under lm-evaluation-harness conventions with length-normalised accuracy where the harness specifies it. Crucially, peer models are re-scored on the same harness rather than compared against published figures. The gap between the two is not negligible: published eighttask means for the peer set run 0.51.5 points above what the same checkpoints score here, because the task subset and normalisation differ. Comparing locally measured number against published one would manufacture roughly point of spurious advantage. Validation bits-per-byte is computed over 645 M-token held-out set. Bits per byte, rather than per token, is used so that the figure is comparable across tokenisersa model with more efficient tokeniser would otherwise appear better at equal predictive quality. B. Decode Decode throughput is measured by generating 128 tokens after priming context of the stated depth, on 8 threads, with 4-bit weights, repeated and reported as mean standard deviation. Two protocol details matter. First, arms alternate within single pass rather than running back to back: an earlier back-to-back measurement in this project produced 1.29 figure that did not reproduce, because background load drifted between the two halves. Second, absolute throughputs are depressed by whatever else shares the machine, so the ratio within pass is the trustworthy quantity and the absolute numbers should be treated as floor.

sections.title: The measurement
sections.content: includes only generation, not prompt processing. Prompt processing is compute-bound and parallel over positions, so it is regime where attention is not disadvantaged; including it would flatter the hybrid on workloads that decode little. XII. DEPLOYMENT NOTES The model targets stock inference binaries with no patches, which constrained several decisions and is worth making explicit for anyone reproducing the deployment. Quantisation format. Q4_0 is chosen over formats with better error characteristics at equal bit width because its dotproduct kernels are the best optimised on the target hardware. The measured quality cost of that choice is 2.5 % perplexity at 5 tokens without quantisation-aware training; the throughput it buys is what the entire design exists to deliver. Formats such as Q4_K would reduce the error and give back part of the speed. attention layers with fixed-state short convolutions buys large speed advantage at no cost in quality. Both halves held. The parameter-matched comparison gave the hybrid the chosen quality metric by 0.81 % against margin fixed in advance, tie on downstream tasks, 6.3 % smaller 4-bit file, and 1.76 faster decoding at 2048 tokens 2.08 against an outside model. The advantage grows with context in every measurement, which is what identifies the cause: model that were simply leaner would be faster by constant. At full scale the model scores 47.31 against bar of 42.20 set before training, beating every model in its size class trained on three to six times more data. Bits-per-byte is 0.8685. What remains open is not the architecture but the engineering around it: 4-bit penalty that quantisation-aware training was meant to remove, roughly half the convolution channels sitting inert because nothing in training discourages that, and vocabulary inherited rather than chosen. None of the three requires new research to fix, and all three are cheaper to address in the next model than to retrofit into this one.

At 2048-token context the keyvalue cache adds approximately 12.6 MB, so complete single-user session fits comfortably under 128 MBsmall enough for the model to be resident alongside an application rather than requiring dedicated process boundary. Thread scaling. All figures here use 8 threads. Because decoding at batch size one is memory-bound, throughput saturates once threads suffice to saturate memory bandwidth; adding cores past that point yields little. The hybrid saturates at lower thread count than the dense twin, since it moves fewer bytes per token, which is secondary benefit on shared machines. XIII. DISCUSSION When the hybrid wins. The advantage is function of context depth. Any deployment that keeps long conversation, retrieves documents into the prompt, or processes files will sit at the right-hand end of Table VII. Deployments that issue short, independent prompts into an empty context will see the depth-0 row and little benefit. Extrapolation beyond 2048. Eq. (4) implies the ratio keeps growing with t, and the measured trend is consistent with that. We decline to quote figure beyond the trained context, because the model has not been trained there and the claim would not be about usable model. Where the ratio could be improved. Two thirds of the layers are already cache-free, so the remaining cache is concentrated in six layers. Reducing attention further trades against retrieval capability, which this experiment did not measure; retrieval-sensitive evaluation is the right instrument for that question and is future work. Future work. Diagnosing the quantisation-aware training failure; addressing dead channels at initialisation rather than export; depth ablation (18 768 against 24 640) which is designed but unrun; multi-seed replication of the ablation; and retrieval-sensitive evaluation to bound how far the attention fraction can fall. XIV. REPRODUCIBILITY Every number in this paper comes from file in the public repository. The head-to-head quality, decode and filesize figures come from the comparisons own results file; the winning condition comes from document timestamped before either model was scored, so it could not have been fitted to the outcome; the five-task and bits-per-byte figures come from the evaluation outputs; and the pruning result comes from script that can be re-run against real model file. The model weights are published at half precision as well as 4-bit, so the quantisation figures can be reproduced and improved on without repeating any training. The corpus is assembled entirely from public datasets. XV. CONCLUSION The proposition was specific and falsifiable: for one user decoding on CPU, replacing two thirds of transformers
